title.ja: edge を理解する: CloudFront Functions、KeyValueStore、Lambda@Edge
title.en: Understand the Edge: CloudFront Functions, KeyValueStore, and Lambda@Edge

sources.title: Restrictions on CloudFront Functions
supports: CloudFront Functions cannot read the request body
The runtime restricts network, file system, environment variable, and timer access
Execution time is limited and reported as compute utilization
Function logs are truncated at 10 KB
KeyValueStore requires JavaScript runtime 2.0
The KeyValueStore API uses SigV4A, which needs version 2 session tokens: use a Regional STS endpoint

sources.title: JavaScript runtime 2.0 features for CloudFront Functions
supports: The runtime is ES 5.1 compliant with selected ES 6 to 12 features; const, let, async, and await are supported in runtime 2.0
No eval or Function constructor, no setTimeout/setImmediate/clearTimeout, no file system, no process, no environment variables, no network calls
Date returns the function's start time for the whole run
console supports only log(), without comma-separated arguments
Built-in modules are buffer, querystring, and crypto
sources.note: The page lists supported features. Syntax it does not list (optional chaining, spread, destructuring, classes, for...of) is treated as unsupported in this book; that inference was not tested on the runtime.

sources.title: CloudFront Functions event structure
supports: A function can return a response with statusCode, headers, and a body given as { encoding, data }
A status of 400 or above returned by a function is not replaced by a custom error page

sources.title: Test functions
supports: CloudFront can run a function against an event object before it is live and report the result, logs, and compute utilization

sources.title: Amazon CloudFront KeyValueStore
supports: Read-only key-value data for CloudFront Functions
Values are strings, byte-encoded strings, or JSON
Intended uses include URL rewrites and redirects, A/B testing and feature flags, and access authorization

sources.title: Helper methods for key value stores
supports: A function starts with `import cf from 'cloudfront'` and `cf.kvs()`
get(key, { format }) rejects when the key does not exist; exists(key) and meta() are the other two methods
Awaiting reads one after another is recommended over promise combinators, which use more memory and are not faster
meta().lastUpdatedDateTime does not include the propagation time to the edge

sources.title: Work with key value data
supports: Pairs in an existing store are changed through the CloudFront KeyValueStore API, which is global and uses SigV4A
Write operations take the store's ETag as If-Match and return a new ETag
The ETags of the CloudFront API and the KeyValueStore API are not interchangeable
UpdateKeys is one all-or-nothing operation
Values are not changed during a function invocation; updates are processed between invocations

sources.title: Create a key value store
supports: A file of pairs can be imported only when the store is first created

sources.title: File format for key-value pairs
supports: Import file limits: 5 MB, 512-character keys, 1024-character values, no duplicate keys

sources.title: CloudFront KeyValueStore API: UpdateKeys
supports: UpdateKeys requires If-Match and returns the new ETag, ItemCount, and TotalSizeInBytes
Listed errors: AccessDenied 403, Conflict 409, InternalServer 500, ResourceNotFound 404, ServiceQuotaExceeded 402, Validation 400
sources.note: The page does not say which error a stale If-Match produces.

sources.title: CloudFront KeyValueStore API: ListKeys
supports: ListKeys returns at most 50 pairs per call (default 10) and a NextToken

sources.title: CloudFront quotas
supports: CloudFront Functions: 10 KB maximum function size (not adjustable), 2 MB maximum function memory, 100 functions per account
Key value stores: 512-byte key, 1 KB value, 5 MB per store, 50 keys or 3 MB per update request, one store per function, 100 functions per store, 200 stores per account
Lambda@Edge: 30-second function timeout, 50 MB compressed size, generated response up to 40 KB (viewer events) or 1 MB (origin events), 10,000 requests per second per Region

sources.title: Differences between CloudFront Functions and Lambda@Edge
supports: CloudFront Functions run on viewer request and viewer response only; Lambda@Edge also on origin request and origin response
CloudFront Functions: submillisecond duration, 2 MB memory, 10 KB code, no network, no file system, no request body
Lambda@Edge: Node.js and Python, up to 30 seconds, network and file system access, request body access, no KeyValueStore

sources.title: Restrictions on all edge functions
supports: One edge function per event type per cache behavior
CloudFront Functions and Lambda@Edge cannot be combined on viewer events; a CloudFront Function on a viewer event with Lambda@Edge on an origin event is allowed
Viewer response functions are not invoked when the origin returns 400 or higher

sources.title: Edge function logs
supports: CloudFront Functions log only console.log() lines, always to us-east-1, in /aws/cloudfront/function/<FunctionName>
Lambda@Edge logs to /aws/lambda/us-east-1.<FunctionName> in the Region where the function ran
Edge function logs are delivered on a best-effort basis

sources.title: Restrictions on Lambda@Edge
supports: The function must be in us-east-1 and must be referenced by a numbered version, not $LATEST or an alias
Not supported: environment variables (other than reserved ones), VPC access, layers, dead letter queues, X-Ray, provisioned concurrency, container images, arm64, more than 512 MB of ephemeral storage
With include body, the body is base64 encoded and truncated at 40 KB (viewer request) or 1 MB (origin request)
The execution role must be assumable by lambda.amazonaws.com and edgelambda.amazonaws.com

sources.title: Set up IAM permissions and roles for Lambda@Edge
supports: Associating a function needs lambda:GetFunction, lambda:EnableReplication*, lambda:DisableReplication*, and iam:CreateServiceLinkedRole
The service-linked roles AWSServiceRoleForLambdaReplicator and AWSServiceRoleForCloudFrontLogger are created automatically

sources.title: Delete Lambda@Edge functions and replicas
supports: A Lambda@Edge function can be deleted only after CloudFront has deleted its replicas, typically within a few hours of removing the last association

sources.title: AWS News Blog: Introducing Amazon CloudFront KeyValueStore
supports: Updates to a store are described as propagating to all edge locations in a few seconds
sources.note: A launch post, not a specification. The Developer Guide pages read for this chapter give no propagation time and no guarantee.

sources.title: Amazon CloudFront pay-as-you-go pricing
supports: Always-free each month: 1 TB data transfer out, 10,000,000 HTTP/HTTPS requests, 2,000,000 CloudFront Function invocations, 2,000,000 KeyValueStore reads
First 1,000 invalidation paths per month are free, then USD 0.005 per path
Origin fetches from AWS origins such as S3 are free of data-transfer charges
KeyValueStore reads from functions cost USD 0.03 per million; other KeyValueStore API actions cost USD 1 per 1,000 requests
Lambda@Edge costs USD 0.60 per million requests and USD 0.00005001 per GB-second, metered per millisecond, with no free tier

sources.title: @aws-sdk/signature-v4a 3.1138.0 (npm registry metadata and package source)
supports: Importing the package registers a JavaScript SigV4A signer that @aws-sdk/signature-v4-multi-region uses when no CRT signer is loaded
sources.note: Read from the installed package and from @aws-sdk/signature-v4-multi-region 3.996.48. The AWS documentation example imports @aws-sdk/signature-v4-crt instead.

sources.title: Cloudflare Workers: Limits
supports: CPU time per HTTP request: 10 ms on Workers Free, 30 seconds by default and up to 5 minutes on Workers Paid; waiting on fetch or KV does not count
128 MB of memory per isolate; Worker size up to 64 MiB uncompressed
Subrequests per invocation: 50 on Free, 10,000 by default on Paid
No hard duration limit for HTTP-triggered Workers while the client stays connected

sources.title: Cloudflare Workers: Pricing
supports: Workers Free: 100,000 requests per day
Workers Standard: 10 million requests and 30 million CPU milliseconds included per month, then USD 0.30 per million requests and USD 0.02 per million CPU milliseconds

sources.title: Cloudflare Workers KV: How KV works
supports: KV is eventually consistent: a change may take up to 60 seconds or more to be visible in other locations
Data is stored centrally and cached at locations after access

sources.title: Cloudflare Workers KV: Limits
supports: Key size 512 bytes, value size 25 MiB, 1 write per second to the same key
A Worker can write to KV; Free allows 1,000 writes per day

sources.title: cdkd v0.296.28: src/provisioning/register-providers.ts
supports: Dedicated providers exist for AWS::S3::Bucket, AWS::S3::BucketPolicy, AWS::CloudFront::OriginAccessControl, AWS::CloudFront::Distribution, AWS::IAM::Role, AWS::IAM::Policy, and AWS::Lambda::Function
No provider is registered for AWS::CloudFront::Function, AWS::CloudFront::KeyValueStore, or AWS::Lambda::Version, so they go through Cloud Control API

sources.title: @go-to-k/cdkd 0.296.28 (npm tarball and tagged source)
supports: Command list, flags, and exit codes used by tools/src/infra and tools/src/drift
`drift --json` output shape (StackDriftJson) and exit codes 0/1/2
`cdkd bootstrap` creates cdkd-state-{account}, cdkd-assets-{account}-{region}, and an ECR repository; it creates no IAM roles and no CDKToolkit stack
Without AWS_REGION cdkd uses us-east-1
A CloudFront distribution is waited for only with --full-wait
State is stored at s3://{bucket}/{prefix}/{stack}/{region}/state.json with an S3 conditional-write lock
AWS::CloudFront::Function is provisioned and read back through Cloud Control API, not a dedicated provider
A non-empty bucket without the CDK auto-delete tag makes destroy fail
AWS::CloudFront::KeyValueStore is in the list of stateful types, whose replacement needs --force-stateful-recreation
Asset publishing uses the stack's own region when the stack sets one (stack.region || base region)
`cdkd local start-cloudfront` serves a distribution locally with its viewer-request functions; --kvs-file backs cf.kvs().get() with a JSON file, and Lambda@Edge is skipped with a warning
sources.note: Read from the published tarball, --help output, and the v0.296.28 source tag. No cdkd command was run against AWS.

definition.ja: CloudFront の edge location で、リクエストやレスポンスのたびに動く小さな JavaScript。ネットワークにもファイルにも触れず、URL やヘッダーの書き換えに使う。
definition.en: Small JavaScript that runs at CloudFront edge locations on each request or response. It cannot reach the network or files and is used to rewrite URLs and headers.

definition.ja: CloudFront が読者からリクエストを受け取った直後、cache を調べる前のタイミング。
definition.en: The moment right after CloudFront receives a request from the reader, before it looks in the cache.

definition.ja: CloudFront Functions から読める、キーと値の保存場所。関数からは読むだけで、書き換えは外から API で行う。
definition.en: A store of key-value pairs that CloudFront Functions can read. Functions only read it; changes come from outside through an API.

definition.ja: us-east-1 に作った Lambda 関数の version を CloudFront が各地に複製し、リクエストの途中で呼ぶ仕組み。
definition.en: A version of a Lambda function created in us-east-1 that CloudFront replicates around the world and invokes partway through a request.

glossary.ja: ETag による条件付き更新

definition.ja: 読んだときの版（ETag）を書き込みに添え、その間に他の誰かが書き換えていたら拒否してもらう方法。
definition.en: Sending the version (ETag) you read along with a write, so the write is refused if someone else changed the data in between.

tiers.description: $6.0E-7  per Request for Lambda-Edge-Request in Asia Pacific (Tokyo)
$0.00005001 per Lambda-GB-Second for Lambda-Edge-GB-Second in Asia Pacific (Tokyo)

allowances.note: Already a USD 0 tier in the price list; listed so the worksheet shows it. Pay-as-you-go only.

unknownAllowances.reason: The pay-as-you-go pricing page lists no free allowance for KeyValueStore API operations; none is applied.

title.ja: edge の例: 月 100 万リクエスト

ja: すべて日本の edge から配信、HTTPS、1 リクエスト平均 20 KB
内訳はトップページ 10%、その他のページ 20%、ファイル 70%。関数はそれぞれ KeyValueStore を 3 回、2 回、1 回読む
CloudFront Function は全リクエストで実行
cache miss と再検証で origin へ 1/3 が届くと仮定
edge:kvs:sync を月 20 回（Describe 1、ListKeys 1、UpdateKeys 1）、edge:kvs:plan を月 10 回（Describe 1、ListKeys 1）
Lambda@Edge は POST /digest の 1 万回だけ。128 MB、平均 50 ミリ秒と仮定
Lambda@Edge のログ（CloudWatch Logs）、標準ログ、WAF、独自ドメインは含まない
en: Served entirely from Japan edge locations over HTTPS, 20 KB per request on average
10% home page, 20% other pages, 70% files; the function reads KeyValueStore 3, 2, and 1 times respectively
The CloudFront Function runs on every request
One third of requests assumed to reach the origin through cache misses and revalidation
edge:kvs:sync 20 times a month (1 Describe, 1 ListKeys, 1 UpdateKeys) and edge:kvs:plan 10 times (1 Describe, 1 ListKeys)
Lambda@Edge runs only for 10,000 POST /digest requests, assumed 128 MB and 50 ms on average
Lambda@Edge logs in CloudWatch Logs, standard logging, WAF, and a custom domain are not included

one third of 1,000,000 requests reach S3 as GET

note.en: The function (the deployed file run under node:vm), KeyValueStore planning and sync, the SDK adapter, the Lambda@Edge handler, and both stacks

summary.ja: 10章の edge-router.js を CloudFront Functions の runtime 2.0 で実行していない。構文、10 KB、2 MB、実行時間（compute utilization）、cf.kvs() を ID なしで呼ぶ形、存在しないキーで get() が reject することは、ドキュメントと Node.js 上のテストでしか確かめていない。
summary.en: Chapter 10's edge-router.js has not run on the CloudFront Functions runtime 2.0. Its syntax, the 10 KB and 2 MB limits, execution time (compute utilization), calling cf.kvs() without an ID, and get() rejecting for a missing key are confirmed only by documentation and tests under Node.js.

resume.ja: vp run edge:infra:deploy の後、aws cloudfront test-function（stage DEVELOPMENT、本文の event）で結果と ComputeUtilization を記録する。続けて edge:publish、edge:kvs:sync を実行し、本文の curl を試す。
resume.en: After vp run edge:infra:deploy, run aws cloudfront test-function (stage DEVELOPMENT, with the event from the chapter) and record the result and ComputeUtilization. Then run edge:publish and edge:kvs:sync and try the chapter's curl commands.

summary.ja: KeyValueStore API が古い If-Match に対して返すエラーの種類を確認していない。API リファレンスは ConflictException（409）を載せているが、どの条件で返るかは書いていない。10章の adapter は ConflictException だけを競合として扱い、それ以外は再試行せずに止まる。
summary.en: Which error the KeyValueStore API returns for a stale If-Match is unconfirmed. The API reference lists ConflictException (409) without saying when it is returned. Chapter 10's adapter treats only ConflictException as a conflict and stops without retrying on anything else.

resume.ja: デプロイ後、aws cloudfront-keyvaluestore put-key を古い ETag の --if-match で実行し、エラー名と状態コードを記録する。ConflictException でなければ examples/10-edge/src/kvs/store.ts の translate と test/store.test.ts を直す。
resume.en: After deploying, run aws cloudfront-keyvaluestore put-key with an old ETag as --if-match and record the error name and status code. If it is not ConflictException, fix translate in examples/10-edge/src/kvs/store.ts and test/store.test.ts.

summary.ja: KeyValueStore の更新が edge に届くまでの時間を計測していない。Developer Guide に数値はなく、AWS News Blog の「a few seconds」だけが手がかり。
summary.en: The time for a KeyValueStore update to reach the edge has not been measured. The Developer Guide gives no figure; the only hint is "a few seconds" in the AWS News Blog.

resume.ja: edge-data.json の maintenance を true にして edge:kvs:sync を実行し、完了時刻から、curl が 503 を返し始めるまでを複数回計る。計った場所と回数を添えて記録する（保証値としては書かない）。
resume.en: Set maintenance to true in edge-data.json, run edge:kvs:sync, and time from its completion until curl starts returning 503, several times. Record it with where and how often it was measured, never as a guarantee.

summary.ja: cdkd 0.296.28 で AWS::CloudFront::KeyValueStore（Cloud Control API 経由、stateful 扱い）と、us-east-1 の stack にある Lambda@Edge 用の関数と AWS::Lambda::Version を実際に作成・更新・削除できるかは未確認。ソースからは、stack 自身のリージョンが使われることと、us-east-1 にも cdkd の asset 置き場が要りそうなことまでしか読み取れていない。Node.js 24 が Lambda@Edge で使えることも個別には確認していない。
summary.en: Whether cdkd 0.296.28 can create, update, and delete AWS::CloudFront::KeyValueStore (through Cloud Control API, treated as stateful) and the Lambda@Edge function and AWS::Lambda::Version in a us-east-1 stack is unconfirmed. The source shows only that the stack's own region is used and that cdkd's asset storage is probably needed in us-east-1 too. Node.js 24 on Lambda@Edge was not confirmed separately either.

resume.ja: AIH_AWS_REGION=us-east-1 vp run infra:bootstrap の後に vp run edge:body:infra:deploy を実行する。出力の BodyDigestVersionArn を -c bodyDigestVersionArn=... で vp run edge:infra:deploy に渡し、curl -X POST で /digest を確かめる。失敗したら内容を記録し、著者に判断を仰ぐ（別のツールへは置き換えない）。
resume.en: Run AIH_AWS_REGION=us-east-1 vp run infra:bootstrap, then vp run edge:body:infra:deploy. Pass the BodyDigestVersionArn output to vp run edge:infra:deploy with -c bodyDigestVersionArn=..., and check /digest with curl -X POST. If it fails, record how and ask the author for a decision; do not substitute another tool.
